name: Sachsen

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this cool ripen Müller-Thurgau, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Pinot Noir and Gewürztraminer fully without cooking off their freshness.
Müller-Thurgau, Riesling, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely. Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Only very early grapes ripen well, mostly hybrids and a few vinifera.
